title: Hello!
text:
I’m Anh Lam, a Chemistry PhD student in Samia Lab at CWRU.
I’m working to become a “hybrid” scientist, handling both experimental and computational projects. If I’m not in the lab or my office working on 10 different projects on nanoparticles, you’ll find me tending to my plants (my growing collection has 12 so far) or doing crafts. I also love pottery making and thrifting. Really, I never run out of things to learn and do!
This website is my personal digital garden for sharing research, projects, notes, and things I’m learning.

title: My Projects
text:
Research Projects
Below are 2 research papers that represent my previous academic work and research interest.


Paper 1
Title: Magnetic field role in solar-driven water evaporation of \(\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}\)/polyvinyl alcohol
This research showed the impact of magnetic strength on the photothermal behavior of the iron oxide-polymer based membranes to increase solar absorption efficiency.
View Magnetic field role in solar-driven water evaporation of Fe3O4/polyvinyl alcohol paper



Paper 2
Title: Carbonized rice husks as absorber materials for solar-driven steam generation devices
This project demonstrated how carbon particles synthesized from rice husk were used as a photothermal material and applied in two solar-driven steam generation systems
View Carbonized rice husks as absorber materials for solar-driven steam generation devices paper
